workflows.preflight:
name: Mobile release preflight

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      platform:
        description: Platform to validate
        required: true
        default: both
        type: choice
        options:
          - android
          - ios
          - both

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  preflight:
    uses: __MOBILE_RELEASE_KIT_REPOSITORY__/.github/workflows/reusable-preflight.yml@__MOBILE_RELEASE_KIT_SHA__
    with:
      tooling_sha: __MOBILE_RELEASE_KIT_SHA__
      source_sha: ${{ github.sha }}
      platform: ${{ inputs.platform }}
workflows.candidate:
name: Mobile internal candidate
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      platform:
        description: Platform to build once and upload to internal testing
        required: true
        type: choice
        options:
        - android
        - ios
        - both
      confirmation:
        description: candidate:<platform>:<version>:<build>
        required: true
        type: string
      recovery_run_id:
        description: Run holding the original intent or selected complete final; never replaces authorization.
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
      recovery_confirmation:
        description: Exact additional iOS recovery confirmation, only when requested by reconciliation.
        required: false
        default: ''
        type: string
permissions: {}
jobs:
  candidate:
    permissions:
      actions: read
      artifact-metadata: write
      attestations: write
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    uses: __MOBILE_RELEASE_KIT_REPOSITORY__/.github/workflows/reusable-candidate.yml@__MOBILE_RELEASE_KIT_SHA__
    with:
      tooling_sha: __MOBILE_RELEASE_KIT_SHA__
      source_sha: ${{ github.sha }}
      platform: ${{ inputs.platform }}
      confirmation: ${{ inputs.confirmation }}
      recovery_run_id: ${{ inputs.recovery_run_id }}
      recovery_confirmation: ${{ inputs.recovery_confirmation }}

inputs.label: Toolkit repository
inputs.what: The GitHub OWNER/REPO containing the shared Mobile Release Kit reusable workflows, not the application repository.
inputs.why: Every caller names this toolkit repository together with an explicit immutable commit; there is no account default.
inputs.where: Open the trusted toolkit repository on GitHub and copy only its owner and repository name from the address. Confirm the intended publisher independently.
inputs.format: OWNER/REPO, for example example/mobile-release-kit. Use the repository coordinate only, not a URL, branch, tag or credential.
inputs.failure: An invalid coordinate rejects the preview. A valid spelling does not verify repository existence, access, publisher identity or workflow compatibility.

inputs.label: Full toolkit commit
inputs.what: The complete 40-hexadecimal commit SHA of the toolkit release you intend the callers to use, not an application source commit.
inputs.why: The same commit is written in both the reusable-workflow reference and tooling_sha so mutable branches or tags cannot silently select another revision.
inputs.where: On the independently trusted toolkit release or commit page, open the commit details and copy the full SHA. Choose a version compatible with the installed core and review that correspondence separately.
inputs.format: Exactly 40 hexadecimal characters. Uppercase is normalized to lowercase. A short SHA, branch, tag or release label is not accepted.
inputs.failure: An invalid pin rejects the preview. This app does not contact GitHub, resolve the SHA or establish that the selected remote workflows match the shipped templates.

inputs.label: Optional supplied comparison
inputs.what: Your own optional absence or byte-length/SHA256 assertions for the four fixed caller files. These are not a snapshot read by this app.
inputs.why: They allow a limited comparison without reading or accepting arbitrary existing workflow text, repository trees or accidental secrets.
inputs.where: Use only a separately obtained summary you intend to compare, or leave comparison unset. Do not paste workflow contents, tokens, keys or credential values here.
inputs.format: For a fixed caller choose not supplied, reported absent, or a reported file length from 0 to 1048576 bytes and its 64-character lowercase SHA256. Omitted callers are unknown, not absent.
inputs.failure: Invalid or duplicate records reject the preview. A matching supplied digest is not proof of file contents, an unchanged repository, a safe no-op, overwrite permission or Apply authority.

guidance.label: Source and toolkit authority
guidance.what: The candidate and production branches shown here are configured policy. The toolkit coordinate and SHA are syntactically pinned inputs only.
guidance.why: A later release must bind actual application source, an authorized repository and compatible immutable toolkit workflows; a draft cannot supply that proof.
guidance.where: Review source.candidateBranch and source.productionBranch in project settings, then have the repository owner establish actual source and protection separately.
guidance.format: Callers retain the literal GitHub source expression and use the same toolkit SHA twice. The schema reference is informational and is not fetched or saved.
guidance.failure: No Git state, repository identity, remote commit, branch protection or installed-template compatibility has been verified. Format-valid never means release-ready.

guidance.label: Protected environments and approvals
guidance.what: The fixed environments are mobile-candidate, mobile-external-testing and mobile-production. Their existing configuration is unknown.
guidance.why: Approvals and stage-specific authority must precede later activation. Production requires reviewed approvers; reviewer identities, branch rules and bypass policy are administrator decisions.
guidance.where: An authorized administrator reviews repository Settings, Environments, Actions permissions and reusable-workflow access before adding authority or activating a caller.
guidance.format: Keep the callers' exact permissions and fixed environment-scoped names. Do not add secrets: inherit or broad repository-write permissions. This checklist is not a GitHub API request.
guidance.failure: No environment, reviewer, branch rule, access permission or secret has been inspected or changed. A generated caller does not establish safe repository setup.

guidance.label: Hosted runner eligibility
guidance.what: Before storing secrets or activating callers, the administrator must ensure no self-hosted runner can match the pinned ubuntu-24.04 or macos-26 labels.
guidance.why: A runner.environment check happens after scheduling. It is defense in depth, not proof that an eligible malicious runner never received a job or credential.
guidance.where: Review actual repository and organization runner inventory and policy with the responsible administrator, and preserve the eligibility restriction.
guidance.format: Use the documented hosted runner scope. This toolkit does not configure a trusted custom runner group or verify runner inventory in this preview.
guidance.failure: A label alone is not trust or server-side scheduling protection. Unverified eligibility remains unresolved even if every generated workflow looks correct.

guidance.label: Names only; keep values private
guidance.what: The requirement list contains only policy-selected credential names, kinds and reasons. All presence, values, correctness and account access remain unknown.
guidance.why: Only candidate receives build-signing assets. External testing and production must not receive a keystore, P12, profile or Firebase client file; Store and build authority stay separated.
guidance.where: Use the administrator's protected environment and secret-management process. Google WIF needs actual immutable repository/environment trust and separately scoped accounts. Apple review-state key generation, retention and rotation are external responsibilities.
guidance.format: Set only the listed fixed environment-scoped names for enabled platforms and conditional Firebase, private-dependency or demo-account needs. Local _PATH alternatives are local guidance, not extra GitHub secret names. Never enter credential values here.
guidance.failure: This app does not read credentials, test access, provision WIF, store secrets or generate keys. Presence is not verification; incomplete operations still require their original private commitment key and version.

guidance.label: Preview does not run a workflow
guidance.what: Even a non-publishing preflight can execute application checks and builds. This preview does not dispatch it or any release operation.
guidance.why: Candidate creation, build-once promotion, production preparation and recovery need the existing source binding, exact confirmations, protected approvals and authenticated evidence.
guidance.where: After separately reviewed setup, use the documented protected workflow lifecycle and retain its real evidence. GitHub App login and guarded desktop dispatch remain unavailable.
guidance.format: Keep every shipped permission, confirmation and recovery input. Production submission selects one platform. Public release is never automated.
guidance.failure: No workflow run, native build, Store request or release evidence is created or authenticated. A successful proposal cannot enable Connect, Apply, secret provisioning or dispatch.

guidance.label: Proposed; nothing applied
guidance.what: This service produces four caller texts and a guidance checklist from a bounded in-memory draft and the shipped templates.
guidance.why: It is useful preparation without project reads, application execution, network access, writes or a misleading claim of repository authority.
guidance.where: Review the read-only proposal alongside its core-owned help. A future real setup operation needs its own authenticated observation, preconditions, explicit confirmation and reconciliation.
guidance.format: The caller convention is release/mobile-release.json. This preview does not generate or save the full init configuration, metadata skeleton or .gitignore transaction.
guidance.failure: A resource error or unavailable runtime remains unavailable, never a fallback to another template source. Generated hashes and supplied comparisons cannot become a repository revision, Apply token or safe retry.
